product_version: Hibernate ORM 6.6.x (Jakarta Persistence 3.1); facts also hold for Hibernate ORM 7.x / Jakarta Persistence 3.2
version_sensitive_claims: FetchType.EAGER does NOT guarantee a JOIN: a direct fetch (em.find) uses a LEFT OUTER JOIN, but an entity/JPQL query without JOIN FETCH loads eager associations with a secondary SELECT — so EAGER may issue a separate SELECT.
In JPA the LAZY strategy is only a HINT to the provider (it may fetch eagerly anyway), whereas EAGER is a requirement that the association be fetched immediately.
Default fetch: @OneToMany/@ManyToMany are LAZY, @ManyToOne/@OneToOne are EAGER (JPA-spec defaults, stable in Hibernate 6.x/7.x).

MultipleBagFetchException is raised when JOIN FETCH-ing two bags (unindexed List). Switching one/both to Set only sidesteps the multiple-bag case; the general N+1/Cartesian fix is separate queries, @BatchSize, JOIN FETCH discipline or @EntityGraph.
Hibernate best practice: mark associations LAZY by default; EAGER is discouraged because it cannot be overridden per query and tends to cause N+1.
Set vs List is a contextual choice (ordering, duplicates, bag-vs-set semantics, MultipleBagFetchException, performance), not a universal winner.
equals/hashCode for entities: use a stable business/natural key when one exists (or a constant hashCode), not all fields — contextual, not an absolute id-only rule.
Hibernate Statistics (SessionFactory.getStatistics()) is a diagnostic you enable when investigating query counts, not a mandatory production setting (it adds overhead).
